description: agent.edit changes an agent row by slug and returns the slug it edited — a daemon write (the agent table, not the closed policy set), so it is registered like loop.create. `fields` is the whole row, because the door is a REPLACEMENT: agentmgr.Edit writes ten content fields wholesale (name, description, functionality, prompt, skills, metadata, avatarType, avatarColor, avatarMood, tools — the tools are checked against the tool registry and a list that names an unknown tool is refused by name; a caller that sends no `tools` leaves the allow-list as it is) and a caller that sends only what its form showed would write the other ones empty (S73 design AR5 — the reason the app's panel loads the row with agent.view first and posts what it loaded). The keys outside those ten are read into the struct and ignored: id, slug, internal, signed and the stamps are the row's, never the caller's, so carrying them costs nothing and changing nothing. A slug with no row is refused by name, so an edit cannot reach an agent that never existed.
